subject: Follow-up: model fit & structured-output evals + next steps

Subject: Follow-up: model fit & structured-output evals + next steps

Thanks for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum:

1) Goals you shared
- High-precision financial entity extraction and enrichment from customer support transcripts
- Deterministic JSON output for downstream billing and audit systems (schema compliance required)
- Low latency (<250ms median for short prompts) and predictable cost for 1M monthly requests

2) Recommended model candidates for evaluation (we'll run the benchmark harness):
- Redwood-Instruct-3B (fast, cost-effective baseline)
- Llama2-13B-chat (good balance of quality/latency)
- Llama2-70B-chat-quant (higher quality, quantized for cost)

3) Focused evals we'll deliver
- JSON schema compliance rate (strict match vs. relaxed parsing)
- Field-level precision/recall on the prompt set you shared today
- Structured output robustness under retries and partial responses
- Latency and cost per 1k tokens across batch sizes

4) Tool/function calling & structured output approach
- We'll evaluate both native function-calling (model->structured payload) and explicit JSON prompt templates (model returns JSON string).
- For function-calling, we'll validate: schema strictness, handling of missing fields, and idempotent retry behavior.
- We'll instrument a lightweight retry policy in the harness: if function-call returns partial/malformed payload, try the configured retry (up to 2) with prompt hints; record success/failure and quiescent latency impact.

5) Risks you flagged
- Possible quality regression after quantization (we'll include quantized variants in the evals)
- Schema drift with edge-case inputs (we'll add adversarial prompts)

Next steps
- I'll drop the initial prompt set and eval harness results in Drive by EOD tomorrow (attachment and link below).
- Can we schedule a 45-min technical deep dive with Marissa and your engineering lead next week? I suggested Tue 9-10am PT — let me know if that works.

Attachments: prompt_set_v1.json (sample prompts), structured_output_eval_report_q2.pdf (template report)

Thanks Rishi — helpful summary. Quick clarifications:

- The schema has two strictly required fields (customer_id, invoice_items) and several optional enrichment fields. We need a strict pass/fail for required fields.
- Our engineering team prefers function-calling if schema guarantees can be met — less parser work on our side.
- For retries: we can afford 1 retry for interactive flows, up to 2 for batch. Latency increase is acceptable for accuracy.

Tom and I are both available Tue 9-10am PT. Please include anyone from engineering who will run the eval harness.

Also: can you include a quick note in the report about how you measure 'JSON compliance' (strict parse vs. semantic match)? That will drive our acceptance criteria.

Subject: RE: Follow-up: model fit & structured-output evals + next steps

Alicia — added some technical detail below on how we'll report compliance and retries. Forwarding the planned eval artifacts (prompt_set_v1.json attached).

How we measure JSON compliance:
- Strict parse: we attempt to parse the model output as JSON; success = valid JSON that validates against your JSON Schema (all required fields present and types match).
- Relaxed/semantic match: if strict parse fails, we apply a deterministic sanitizer (quote-fix, trailing commas, common numbering formats) and attempt re-parse; if still failing, we run a heuristic field-extractor to compute whether the semantic values are present (e.g., customer_id found as free text).

Retry policy in the harness:
- Function-calling path: on malformed response or missing required fields, we run 1 automatic retry with a short prompt hint ("Return only valid JSON for the schema: <link>"). We log both attempts and final outcome.
- Prompt-template path: same retry behavior but we include a stricter format hint and explicit 'If you cannot return valid JSON, return ERROR with reason' to reduce hallucinations.

Metrics we'll include in the report:
- Strict JSON pass rate (primary acceptance metric)
- Post-sanitizer pass rate (secondary)
- Required-field pass rate (per-field precision/recall)
- Retry success delta (how many failures converted to passes due to retry)
- Latency & cost delta per model variant and per-retry
- Example failure cases and suggested prompt/instruction tweaks

I'll run the first batch of 200 prompts across the three model candidates and share the CSV/drive link by tomorrow EOD. For the deep dive, Marissa (SE) will walk through failure modes and suggested mitigations; Lauren (CS) will discuss rollout and SLA considerations.
